mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 0.3% month-over-month signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL increases > 0.3% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2 percentage points over 3 months signals a strengthening labor market, which is typically associated with positive economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where RSAFS increases over three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over 3 months signals a weakening supply side, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where INDPRO decreases > 1% in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals a tightening monetary policy with high inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
regime_hint: high inflation with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 5% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over 3 months, coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2 percentage points, signals a robust labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200k in 3 months and UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS increases > 200k in 3 months and UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Housing Starts (HOUST) by more than 10% over 3 months signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where HOUST decreases > 10% in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter signals strong economic growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where GDPC1 increases > 2% QoQ.
